## **1\. Directive 1: Formal Sign-Off on the Substrate Purity Decision**

### **1.1 Architectural Evaluation of Document 04 (ws-hermes vs. \~/.hermes/)**

Lead Architect Argon formally ratifies the core architectural determination presented in Document 04 (04\_doc4\_ws\_hermes\_icm\_architecture\_plan\_asd\_ste100.md): the /var/home/imshubhamsocial/.hermes/ directory and its embedded git submodule /var/home/imshubhamsocial/.hermes/hermes-agent must remain **100% in their pristine upstream form**, while the external workspace /var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes/ (ws-hermes) is structured as a 5-layer Interpretable Context Methodology (ICM) filesystem state machine2.  
This strict boundary resolves the tension between rapid agent harness updates and deterministic workflow state management. During Epoch 4 (GDR26–GDR29, Phases 26–53), the engineering team purged 17 bespoke Python and shell wrapper scripts (mcp\_ephemeral\_bridge.py, ast\_canonizer.py, and related ad-hoc glue) that had accumulated inside the repository3. Reorganizing \~/.hermes/ into numbered ICM stage folders would violate the internal directory layout expected by the NousResearch Hermes runtime—specifically hermes\_cli, the package manager (pm) Python environment generations under installs/INSTALL\_KEY/environments/, state.db SQLite session storage, and plugins/ discovery—and would trigger merge conflicts on every upstream git pull2.  
Maintaining this separation directly implements ICM Principle 5 (*"Configure the factory, not the product"*) and RinDig/icm-architect Invariant 5 (*"Factory vs. Product separation"*)2. In our topology, \~/.hermes/ functions strictly as the **Execution Engine** (hosting the terminal toolset, FastMCP dynamic bridge, openviking Port 1933 memory graph plugin, jev-curator guardrail engine, and TUI/CLI binaries), whereas ws-hermes functions as the **Declarative Software Factory** (holding Layer 0–2 routing contracts, Layer 3 reference rules, and Layer 4 stage deliverables)2. Because ws-hermes relies exclusively on plain directories, Markdown contracts (AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md), and standard POSIX/Python verification scripts in \_tools/, the workspace remains vendor-neutral and can be navigated cold by Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini CLI without modifying a single line of engine code5.

### **1.2 Verification of skills.external\_dirs, Security Scanner Behavior, and hermes \--tui Mechanics**

Our review of the upstream NousResearch Hermes Agent documentation (website/docs/user-guide/features/skills.md, docs/user-guide/tui, and docs/user-guide/cli) confirms that connecting \~/.hermes/ to ws-hermes via skills.external\_dirs and hermes \--tui satisfies all operational requirements, provided four upstream implementation mechanics are enforced2.  
First, upstream Hermes Agent resolves skills across four directory tiers in strict decreasing order of precedence: project \-\> local (\~/.hermes/skills/) \-\> skills.create\_dir \-\> skills.external\_dirs8. Skills located in skills.external\_dirs appear in the system prompt index, skills\_list(), skill\_view(), \-s / \--skills preloading, and /skill-name slash commands identically to local skills6. However, because external\_dirs sits at the lowest precedence tier, any skill with an identical name inside \~/.hermes/skills/ silently shadows the copy in ws-hermes/skills/8. Workspace skills (icm-architect, icm-stage-compiler, ast-grep-auditor) must therefore reside only in the configured external directories (/var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes/skills and /var/home/imshubhamsocial/.agents/skills) and never be duplicated into \~/.hermes/skills/2.  
Second, we must account for the Hermes Skills Hub security scanner behavior when installing RinDig/icm-architect. Document 04 Section 2.1 suggests running hermes skills install https\://github.com/RinDig/icm-architect2. However, practitioner reports from the Clief Notes community (20) and upstream Hermes security documentation (8) show that running hermes skills install on RinDig/icm-architect triggers a DANGEROUS scanner quarantine verdict (agent\_config\_mod in references/system-map.md, line 61\) because the skill teaches the agent how to write AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md files and references parent-relative paths such as ../../\_shared/voice.md8. When quarantined by the Hub installer, the skill is omitted from skills\_list and blocked from slash-command execution8. Cloning RinDig/icm-architect via git clone into /var/home/imshubhamsocial/.agents/skills/icm-architect and /var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes/skills/icm-architect and registering those paths under skills.external\_dirs in \~/.hermes/config.yaml is the official upstream installation method specified in the RinDig/icm-architect README8. Moreover, external skill directories are exempt from autonomous modification or deletion by the Hermes curator background maintenance job8.  
Third, upstream Hermes documentation notes that skills.external\_dirs is not an automatic write-protection boundary: if an external skill directory is writable by the Hermes OS user, agent-invoked skill\_manage calls (patch, write\_file, remove\_file, delete) can modify those skill files in place8. To protect factory rules against accidental mutation during runtime execution, shared skills cloned into \~/.agents/skills/icm-architect must be marked read-only at the filesystem level (chmod \-R a-w \~/.agents/skills/icm-architect)8.  
Fourth, launching hermes \--tui from /var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes provides a terminal user interface that automatically loads root AGENTS.md, streams thinking and tools blocks inline, tracks the active git branch on the status bar, and displays the session auto-compression counter (🗜️ N)2. However, as documented in the Document 02 infrastructure forensics (Konsole TTY Stripping), hermes \--tui requires an active pseudo-terminal (/dev/pts/\*) and exits immediately with hermes-tui: no TTY if stdin is redirected from /dev/null4. Therefore, interactive human sessions, Walk Tests, and checkpoint reviews must use hermes \--tui attached to an active /dev/pts/\* pseudo-terminal (with display.interface: tui set in \~/.hermes/config.yaml), whereas automated headless pipeline runs (Makefile and \_tools/hermes\_stage\_runner.py) must invoke hermes chat \--query-file \<stage\_prompt\_file\> in a non-interactive child process2.

### **1.3 Three Mandatory Adjustments to the Document 04 Schema and Configuration**

To align Document 04 with the empirical findings of GDR30–GDR35 and upstream ICM invariants, we mandate three specific adjustments before sealing the workspace architecture.  
First, \~/.hermes/config.yaml must be upgraded to \_config\_version: 46 to reflect the GDR30 benchmark certification2. In Document 04 Section 2, the sample config.yaml (v45) still listed default: gemma-4-E4B-it-qat2. However, GDR30 (Document 01 Sections 4.1, 4.2, and 7\) demonstrated that Candidate 1 (google/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-q4\_0-gguf) suffered from QAT logit degradation, hallucinated non-existent tool names (find\_user\_id\_by, transfer\_to\_human\_agent) and order IDs (\#W2378155), and scored 0.000 (0/2 passed, 0.0%) on Tau-Bench Retail, resulting in its permanent deprecation for agentic tool use3. Conversely, Candidate 3 (unsloth/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-UD-Q4\_K\_XL.gguf) achieved 60.0% strict pass (3/5) and 100% output match (5/5 tasks, including complex 3-item returns and 10-shirt conditional exchanges) on Tau-Bench Retail and solved GAIA Level 1 orbital mechanics (17,000 hours) on Turn 1 while utilizing 4,975 MiB VRAM (+825 MiB safety margin below the 5,800.0 MiB hardware ceiling)1. Candidate 2 (xbill9/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-q4\_0-exact.gguf) achieved 66.7% (2/3 passed) on Tau-Bench at 4,169 MiB VRAM (+1,631 MiB headroom) and serves as the Tier 1A ultra-lean fallback3. Accordingly, config.yaml v46 sets nemotron-3.5-bolt-e4b-ud-q4\_k\_xl as model.default, gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-exact as model.fallback, display.interface: tui, and tool\_loop\_guardrails.non\_interactive\_hard\_stop\_enabled: true3.  
![][image1]  
Second, we resolve the Layer 0 dual-file duplication between AGENTS.md and IDENTITY.md in Document 04 Section 32. In RinDig/icm-architect, Invariant 2 (*"A small, stable entry file"*) and Invariant 8 (*"One Fact, One Home"*) classify *"Duplicated entry files that drift"* as an explicit anti-pattern5. As Ryan McKinney (RyMac at filesnfolders.com) observed in live ICM audits, storing workspace maps in two root files causes inevitable divergence where the LLM picks one silently without raising an error24. Following the current RinDig/icm-architect cross-agent specification (15), **AGENTS.md is designated the sole canonical Layer 0 file** (\<60 lines) at /var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes/AGENTS.md, while IDENTITY.md and CLAUDE.md are retained strictly as 1-line compatibility pointers (Read AGENTS.md for workspace identity, system invariants, and Layer 1 routing (CONTEXT.md).)9.  
Third, we add explicit support for output/check.md (automated verification receipt), output/checkpoint.md (human review gate state file), and \_archive/ (holding retired Dead files verified to have zero live referrers during icm-architect Restructure Mode) to the workspace directory schema and \_templates/ folder2.

## **2\. Directive 2: Verification of Gauntlet Remediations and the "Green Audit, Broken Runtime" Gap**

### **2.1 Forensic Certification of Frontier Gauntlets A, B, and C**

Having audited the chronological engineering forensics in Document 02 (02\_doc2\_gdr30\_to\_gdr35\_chronological\_implementations\_issues\_and\_forensics.md), Lead Architect Argon certifies that all runtime defects across Gauntlets A, B, and C have been diagnosed at the root-cause level, remediated cleanly without bespoke framework bloat, and verified in live Playwright browser sessions1.  
In **Gauntlet A (benchmarks/gauntlet\_a\_voxel\_fps/ — 3D Voxel FPS & 20 Hz Netcode)**, the engineering team resolved seven compounding runtime failures1. Most notably, in voxel\_world.js line 75, the color-channel unpack expression (hexColor \>\> 16\) & 0xFF / 255.0 failed silently because in ECMAScript operator precedence, division (/) binds tighter than bitwise AND (&)1. JavaScript evaluated 0xFF / 255.0 first (1.0), and then evaluated (hexColor \>\> 16\) & 1.0, which coerced 1.0 to the 32-bit integer 1 and masked only the least significant bit of the channel (for example, 136 & 1 \= 0), rendering every voxel pure black1. Restoring explicit parentheses (((hexColor \>\> 16\) & 0xFF) / 255.0) restored vivid RGB floats1. In addition, the team packed 1,042 continuous solid voxels into the Three.js instance buffer, added a sky-blue atmosphere (0x87CEEB) and hemisphere lighting, moved the camera spawn inside the arena to (16, 2.5, 20\) (instead of spawning facing \-Z into the void while terrain sat at \+X, \+Z), wired a click listener on \#overlay to invoke controls.lock(), updated obsolete Three.js r164 CDN importmaps to valid unpkg and jsdelivr endpoints for PointerLockControls.js, removed a duplicate connectWebSocket() call in main.js, and standardized WebSocket packet handling in socket\_sync.js (\`data.type \|  
\| data.t) to reconcile WELCOMEandjoinat a 20 Hz server broadcast rate1. Live Playwright verification confirmed 0 console errors, 0 page errors,1280x720canvas rendering, andcontract.shexit code0\`1.  
In **Gauntlet B (benchmarks/gauntlet\_b\_splatbox/ & stages/01-probe..03-execute — Splatbox 3D Paintball CV)**, the team restructured the workflow into a 3-stage ICM compiler pipeline1. Replacing the sandboxed agent-browser wrapper with native Playwright connect\_over\_cdp("http\://127.0.0.1:9222") eliminated CDP connection timeouts and attached in 12 ms4. Scaling detected centroids by the CSS-to-canvas pixel ratio (canvas.width / rect.width) eliminated High-DPI aiming drift4. Executing OpenCV HoughCircles on the host CPU required \< 5 ms per frame and 0 MiB GPU VRAM while maintaining \< 5 px aiming error, capturing 145 frames (\>= 100 required), achieving score \= 1 in 58.2s, and passing contract.sh with exit code 01.  
In **Gauntlet C (benchmarks/gauntlet\_c\_aquarium/ — 3D WebGL Aquarium GPGPU & Boids)**, the team fixed a Three.js CDN 404 error by updating three@r165 to three@0.165.0 and diagnosed a silent Three.js ShaderMaterial schema bug in both caustics\_shader.js and water\_gpgpu.js, where singular uniform: { ... } was passed instead of plural uniforms: { ... }1. Because JavaScript accepts arbitrary keys on object literals, static syntax checks passed while Three.js ignored the custom shader uniforms at runtime and logged console warnings1. Replacing uniform: with uniforms: cleared all warnings, and populating main.js with a marine background (0x02162e), lighting, sandy bed (0xd2b48c), cyan glass wireframe boundary (0x00ffff), water surface (0x00b4d8), 15 vivid boid fish (0xff6b35, 0x00f5d4, 0xffd166), the clamped-buoyancy physics sphere (sphere\_physics.js), and HUD buttons produced a complete 3D marine scene verified in live Playwright with 0 console errors, 0 warnings, 1280x720 canvas rendering, and contract.sh exit code 01.

### **2.2 Architectural Analysis: Why the "Green Audit, Broken Runtime" Gap Occurs**

A central forensic insight from GDR30 through GDR35 is the **"Green Audit, Broken Runtime" Gap**: a failure mode in which deterministic unit tests (node test.js) and static AST/regex contracts (ast-grep, grep) pass 100% (exit 0\) while the actual interactive browser runtime renders a black void, fails to fetch ES modules over HTTP, or drops WebSocket packets1.  
This gap arises because static AST audits and isolated unit tests verify **syntactic token presence and isolated mathematical functions**, whereas a browser application requires **end-to-end network resolution, WebGL state binding, camera-frustum alignment, and client-server protocol synchronization**. Five structural decouplings explain why static contracts pass while the runtime fails:

| Failure Mode Category | Static / Unit Audit Assumption (Why It Passed Green) | Actual Browser Runtime Reality (Why It Failed Silently) | Concrete GDR30–GDR35 Forensic Instance |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Operator Precedence vs. Token Presence** | Regex/AST checks confirm that \>\> 16, & 0xFF, and / 255.0 exist on the color extraction line1. | JS evaluates / before &, computing 136 & 1 \= 0 and zeroing out RGB channels1. | Gauntlet A (voxel\_world.js line 75): Voxels rendered pure black despite passing token checks1. |
| **2\. Dynamic Object Schema Silence** | JS/AST parsers verify that new THREE.ShaderMaterial({...}) is syntactically valid ECMAScript1. | Three.js ignores unknown key uniform: (singular), leaving GLSL uniforms unbound and logging a browser console warning1. | Gauntlet C (caustics\_shader.js, water\_gpgpu.js): Shaders failed to bind uniforms1. |
| **3\. Offline AST vs. DOM Network Resolution** | Local ast-grep inspects \<script type="importmap"\> strings without making HTTP requests4. | Browser fetches obsolete CDN URLs (three@r165), receives HTTP 404, and aborts ES module graph execution4. | Gauntlets A & C (index.html): Broken CDN paths halted scene initialization4. |
| **4\. Isolated Math vs. Framebuffer State** | Unit tests validate sphere\_physics.js buoyancy math in Node.js without a WebGL context4. | main.js spawns 0 instances or aims the camera at \-Z away from \+X, \+Z geometry, rendering a uniform black/empty canvas1. | Gauntlets A & C: Empty voxel buffer, unspawned boid fish, and camera facing void1. |
| **5\. Single-File Check vs. Protocol Handshake** | Static checks verify server.js broadcasts JSON and socket\_sync.js parses JSON independently4. | Server sends type: "join" while client switches on type: "WELCOME", and main.js opens duplicate sockets1. | Gauntlet A (socket\_sync.js, main.js): Unknown message type: undefined in console4. |

### **2.3 Immutable Contract Standard: The 4-Gate Headless Browser Runtime Verification Protocol**

To close the "Green Audit, Broken Runtime" Gap permanently across all Hermes Agent OS stages, we codify **Invariant 11 (The 4-Gate Runtime & Framebuffer Contract)**: *No stage or benchmark producing a browser, DOM, Canvas, or WebGL artifact may be marked PASS based solely on static AST/regex checks or isolated Node.js unit tests.* Every contract.sh for an interactive or visual workload must invoke \_tools/playwright\_runtime\_audit.py to verify four runtime gates inside a live headless Chromium instance (1280x720 viewport)1:

> 1. **Gate 1 (Zero Console Error, Page Error, and WebGL Warning Gate)**: Attach listeners to page.on("console") and page.on("pageerror"). Any console.error, uncaught pageerror, or THREE.WebGLProgram / THREE.ShaderMaterial warning causes an immediate non-zero exit (exit 1\)1.  
> 2. **Gate 2 (Zero HTTP 4xx/5xx Asset & Importmap Resolution Gate)**: Attach a listener to page.on("response"). Any HTTP status \>= 400 on HTML, JS ES modules, importmaps, textures, or shaders causes an immediate exit 14.  
> 3. **Gate 3 (DOM Canvas Geometry & High-DPI Ratio Gate)**: Query the target \<canvas\> element, verify that it is attached and visible in the DOM, and assert that its bounding box equals 1280x720 (or the contract-specified dimensions) with a positive, finite canvas.width / rect.width scale factor1.  
> 4. **Gate 4 (Framebuffer Pixel Variance & Non-Black-Void Gate)**: After allowing the render loop (requestAnimationFrame) to execute for a deterministic warmup interval (1,500 ms), capture a lossless PNG buffer of the \<canvas\> and compute its RGB pixel standard deviation using NumPy and OpenCV. If the RGB standard deviation is less than 5.0 (indicating a solid black screen, solid background void, or unrendered scene), the audit fails with exit 11.

Save the following drop-in replacement script to /var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes/\_tools/playwright\_runtime\_audit.py (strictly under 60 lines, zero placeholders)1:

Python  
\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
"""Immutable 4-Gate Headless Browser Runtime & Framebuffer Verifier."""  
import argparse  
import json  
import sys  
import numpy as np  
import cv2  
from playwright.sync\_api import sync\_playwright

def run\_audit(url: str, width: int, height: int, min\_std: float, out\_json: str) \-\> int:  
    console\_errors, page\_errors, bad\_http, warnings \= \[\], \[\], \[\], \[\]  
    with sync\_playwright() as p:  
        browser \= p.chromium.launch(headless=True)  
        page \= browser.new\_page(viewport={"width": width, "height": height})  
        page.on("console", lambda m: console\_errors.append(m.text) if m.type \== "error" else (  
            warnings.append(m.text) if m.type \== "warning" else None))  
        page.on("pageerror", lambda exc: page\_errors.append(str(exc)))  
        page.on("response", lambda r: bad\_http.append(f"{r.status}:{r.url}") if r.status \>= 400 else None)  
        page.goto(url, wait\_until="networkidle", timeout=15000)  
        page.wait\_for\_timeout(1500)  
        canvas \= page.locator("canvas").first  
        box \= canvas.bounding\_box() if canvas.count() \> 0 else None  
        png\_bytes \= canvas.screenshot() if box else b""  
        browser.close()  
    img \= cv2.imdecode(np.frombuffer(png\_bytes, np.uint8), cv2.IMREAD\_COLOR) if png\_bytes else None  
    pixel\_std \= float(np.std(img)) if img is not None else 0.0  
    geom\_ok \= bool(box and int(round(box\["width"\])) \== width and int(round(box\["height"\])) \== height)  
    passed \= (len(console\_errors) \== 0 and len(page\_errors) \== 0 and len(bad\_http) \== 0  
              and len(warnings) \== 0 and geom\_ok and pixel\_std \>= min\_std)  
    receipt \= {"url": url, "passed": passed, "console\_errors": len(console\_errors),  
               "page\_errors": len(page\_errors), "warnings": len(warnings),  
               "http\_4xx\_5xx": len(bad\_http), "canvas\_box": box, "pixel\_std": round(pixel\_std, 2)}  
    if out\_json:  
        with open(out\_json, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
            json.dump(receipt, f, indent=2)  
    print(json.dumps(receipt))  
    return 0 if passed else 1

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
    ap \= argparse.ArgumentParser()  
    ap.add\_argument("--url", required=True)  
    ap.add\_argument("--width", type\=int, default=1280)  
    ap.add\_argument("--height", type\=int, default=720)  
    ap.add\_argument("--min-std", type\=float, default=5.0)  
    ap.add\_argument("--out", default="")  
    args \= ap.parse\_args()  
    sys.exit(run\_audit(args.url, args.width, args.height, args.min\_std, args.out))

## **3\. Directive 3: Validation of Upstream ICM Specifications, Agentless Paradigm, and Video Corpus**

### **3.1 Audit of the Upstream GitHub Repositories (RinDig and ktnCodes)**

We have verified the extraction in Document 03 (03\_doc3\_jake\_van\_clief\_icm\_theory\_specifications\_and\_github\_manifest.md) against the foundational paper (*Interpretable Context Methodology: Folder Structure as Agentic Architecture*, Jake Van Clief & David McDermott, Eduba & University of Edinburgh, arXiv:2603.16021v2, March 18, 2026\) and the four upstream GitHub repositories5.  
In **RinDig/Interpretable-Context-Methodology**, ICM grounds AI context management in 1970s Unix pipeline design (McIlroy, 1978: small programs doing one thing well, output of one stage becoming input of the next, plain text as the universal interface), Stuart Feldman's Make build systems (1979: files on disk serving as both working artifacts and dependency-graph coordination), David Parnas's information-hiding modular decomposition (1972), and Edsger Dijkstra's separation of concerns10. Crucially, the authors note that ICM is complementary to Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP): whereas MCP standardizes how an AI model accesses external tools and data sources (such as our openviking Port 1933 memory graph), ICM operates on the workflow layer to scope which context files and MCP tool definitions are loaded at each stage, avoiding token bloat3. At the same time, both arXiv:2603.16021v2 and foldersoveragents.com explicitly note ICM's scope boundaries: ICM is optimized for sequential, human-reviewed, repeatable workflows and is not intended for high-concurrency multi-tenant queues, real-time inter-agent message-passing loops, or complex automated mid-pipeline branching9.  
Every compliant ICM workspace enforces the **15 Core Conventions** defined in \_core/CONVENTIONS.md (https\://raw.githubusercontent.com/RinDig/Interpretable-Context-Methodology/main/\_core/CONVENTIONS.md), which we codify for ws-hermes in the reference matrix below1:

| Convention Category | ID & Pattern Name | Operational Specification in \_core/CONVENTIONS.md |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Architecture Patterns** | **1\. Stage contracts** | Every stage CONTEXT.md explicitly defines three sections: Inputs, Process, and Outputs5. |
| **Architecture Patterns** | **2\. Stage handoffs** | Stage output/ folders connect pipeline steps; human edits in output/ are read directly by the next stage10. |
| **Architecture Patterns** | **3\. One-way references** | Dependencies flow strictly one way (if Stage A references B, B never references A) to prevent circularity13. |
| **Architecture Patterns** | **4\. Selective section routing** | Stage Inputs tables specify exact markdown sections to load rather than reading entire files5. |
| **Architecture Patterns** | **5\. Canonical sources** | Every fact or rule lives in a single authoritative location ("One Fact, One Home") to prevent drift9. |
| **Quality Patterns** | **6\. Specs are contracts** | Specification stages define *WHAT* and *WHEN*, giving build stages freedom for *HOW* within Layer 3 rules13. |
| **Quality Patterns** | **7\. Checkpoints** | Creative or direction-setting stages pause execution for human steering between major steps13. |
| **Quality Patterns** | **8\. Stage audits** | Pre-output quality checklists run with explicit binary pass conditions before emitting final output13. |
| **Quality Patterns** | **9\. Value validation** | Content and data stages explicitly lock output value types and schemas prior to drafting13. |
| **Quality Patterns** | **10\. Docs over outputs** | Agents read static Layer 3 reference documents for patterns rather than prior Layer 4 outputs, preventing error compounding3. |
| **Onboarding Patterns** | **11\. Questionnaire design** | Onboarding questionnaires (setup/questionnaire.md) are flat, executed all-at-once, and configure system settings5. |
| **Onboarding Patterns** | **12\. Shared constants** | Workspaces generating code maintain centralized constant/invariant files so updates propagate globally13. |
| **Structural Patterns** | **13\. Strict line limits** | All CONTEXT.md files must remain under 80 lines; Layer 3 reference files must remain under 200 lines13. |
| **Structural Patterns** | **14\. Clean output state** | Stage output/ directories do not commit generated run artifacts to git (retaining .gitkeep templates)13. |
| **Structural Patterns** | **15\. System-level setup scoping** | Setup extracts concrete examples and configures the production factory once rather than per run5. |

In **ktnCodes/icm-template** (https\://raw.githubusercontent.com/ktnCodes/icm-template/master/README.md), we validate the three maintenance skills (/icm-scaffold, /icm-sync, /icm-context-scaffold), the distinction between **Quick Mode** (3 layers overlaid onto an existing code project without moving existing folders) and **Full Mode** (5 layers with physical stage directories), and the **Karpathy LLM Knowledge Base Compilation Metaphor** (Raw \-\> Layer 4 unstructured source inputs; Compile \-\> Stage 2 compilation using a section-to-source mapping table; Wiki \-\> Layer 4 cross-referenced output articles; Q\&A \-\> Layer 1 index routing)1.  
In **RinDig/icm-architect** (https\://raw.githubusercontent.com/RinDig/icm-architect/main/SKILL.md), we validate the **10 Invariants**, the **3 Primitives** (*Sequence*, *Shelf*, *Catalog*), the **6 Workspace Forms** documented in references/forms.md (*Pipeline*, *Umbrella*, *Record Library*, *Knowledge Bundle*, *Context Map*, and *System Map*), **Build Mode** (5 steps from dialogue extraction to Walk Test), and **Restructure Mode** (7 sequential steps: non-destructive tree inventory, hidden form discovery, 5-role file classification into Catalog, Contract, Factory, Product, and Dead, reference-integrity check across in-vault, ../, symlink, and external consumers, human approval gate on the migration map, copy-verify-remove migration checking case-folding collisions, and cold Walk Test validation)1.

### **3.3 Evaluation of "Method Document vs. Worker with Capabilities" (RinDig/agentless) and the 54-Word vs. 4,115-Word Empirical Finding**

The RinDig/agentless specification (https\://raw.githubusercontent.com/RinDig/agentless/main/README.md) formulates the foundational design premise of our workspace:  
*"An agent package is not a worker with capabilities. It is a method document."*1  
In heavyweight agent frameworks such as Agentlas OS, developers bundle *workflow method* inside *Python capability wrappers*, requiring 2,058 files, 339,886 lines of Python code, 88 JSON schemas, and 28 to 31 mandatory files per package5. However, an agent harness like Hermes Agent already provides the underlying execution capabilities (POSIX bash toolset, file read/edit tools, ast-grep, Playwright CDP browser automation, and FastMCP connections)3. What the model requires per workflow is not another Python daemon, but a **Method Document**—implemented in agentless using just 225 lines of Markdown across SKILL.md and seven starter templates, with zero Python dependencies and zero JSON schemas5.  
![][image2]  
In the empirical benchmark reported in the RinDig/agentless documentation, a **54-word instruction** pointing at external rule files scored **7.00 out of 7** across two test models, whereas a **652-word instruction** scored **6.33 and 5.00**, and a **4,115-word instruction** (with full rule sheets pasted inline) dropped to **5.67 and 6.00**5. While foldersoveragents.com notes that broader ICM practitioner workflows rely primarily on field reporting rather than large-scale clinical trials, this specific instruction-length experiment illustrates a fundamental property of causal transformer attention5. In a standard scaled dot-product attention layer with query vector ![][image3] at generation step ![][image4] and key vectors ![][image5], the attention weight assigned to token ![][image6] is:  
![][image7]  
When a 4,115-word prompt (approximately 5,500 tokens) pastes every rule, style guide, and edge-case constraint inline before execution begins, the denominator sums over thousands of competing tokens simultaneously, diluting the attention probability mass allocated to the specific step currently executing and inducing the *"Lost in the Middle"* recall degradation documented by Liu et al. (\[25\] in arXiv:2603.16021v2)3. Conversely, when the initial prompt is a 54-word pointer directive, the model starts with clean routing intent and invokes read\_file to load only the specific section required for the current step, placing those rules at the immediate recency frontier of the context window3.  
This mechanism also explains the interplay between our **131,072-token (128K) physical llama-server buffer** and ICM's **2,000–8,000 token active prompt budget**3. Across every stage, Layers 0 through 2 contribute roughly **1,300 to 1,600 tokens** of identity, routing, and stage contract instructions (\~800 \+ \~300 \+ 200–500), while Layer 3 adds **500 to 2,000 tokens** of selectively loaded reference material5. Keeping the core stage instruction window between 2,000 and 8,000 tokens preserves peak instruction adherence while leaving over 120,000 tokens of physical KV-cache capacity in llama-server to absorb large intermediate tool outputs (such as ast-grep syntax trees or compiler traces) within our 5,800.0 MiB VRAM ceiling3.

### **3.4 Affirmation of the 8-Point ICM Walk Test as a Mandatory Release Criterion**

Lead Architect Argon formally ratifies **The Walk Test** (specified in RinDig/icm-architect and RinDig/agentless) as a mandatory release gate for all stages and benchmarks in ws-hermes1. No phase may be sealed in phases/status\_ledger.json unless a cold agent with zero conversational memory—and our static linter \_tools/hermes\_icm\_validator.py—passes all eight checks of the Walk Test2:

> 1. **Entry Point Check (\<= 3 Reads to Action)**: Opening the workspace root, can a cold agent answer *where am I* and *where do I go for task X* using AGENTS.md plus at most two additional reads (CONTEXT.md and stages/{NN}/CONTEXT.md)5?  
> 2. **Contract Completeness Check**: Does every working stage and benchmark folder contain a CONTEXT.md (\<80 lines) that explicitly names exact Inputs paths (split into working vs. reference), numbered Process steps, Outputs path/format, and the Check / Human Gate5?  
> 3. **Disk State Observability Check**: Can pipeline completion status be determined entirely by inspecting files in output/ (output/check.md, output/checkpoint.md) and phases/status\_ledger.json without querying an external database or chat history5?  
> 4. **Zero-Payload Catalog Check**: Are Layer 0 (AGENTS.md, \<60 lines) and Layer 1 (CONTEXT.md, \<80 lines) strictly routing catalogs holding zero bulky reference payloads5?  
> 5. **Single Home Check ("One Fact, One Home")**: Is every system invariant stored in a single canonical file (\_config/invariants.md) with relative links replacing duplicate copies, and are CLAUDE.md and IDENTITY.md 1-line pointers to AGENTS.md9?  
> 6. **Reference & Link Integrity Check**: Do all relative file paths (../, ../../\_config/, ../../shared/) in every CONTEXT.md resolve to existing files on disk, with zero circular stage dependencies (Convention 3: One-way references)2?  
> 7. **Token & Line Budget Check**: Does the combined token footprint of AGENTS.md \+ root CONTEXT.md \+ stage CONTEXT.md \+ scoped Inputs remain within the **2,000–8,000 token** working envelope (with CONTEXT.md files \< 80 lines and reference files \< 200 lines)3?  
> 8. **System Map Impact Check**: For any codebase directory that later agents edit (benchmarks/gauntlet\_a\_voxel\_fps/, benchmarks/gauntlet\_c\_aquarium/), can a cold agent identify *what component X is* and *what else moves if X changes* from its stage CONTEXT.md and shared/ reference cards9?

## **4\. Directive 4: Industrial Software Factory Design for Autonomous Pipelines**

### **4.1 Autonomous Multi-Stage Chaining Without Context Leakage**

In an industrial ICM software factory, multi-stage pipelines (such as Gauntlet B's 01-probe/ \-\> 02-controller/ \-\> 03-execute/) must chain across stage boundaries without leaking intermediate reasoning traces, failed tool retries, or stale assumptions from Stage k into Stage k+11.  
To prevent context leakage across stage boundaries, we prohibit executing multiple pipeline stages inside a single continuous chat session. Instead, \_tools/hermes\_stage\_runner.py enforces process-level and context-level isolation across every transition. Each stage is compiled by spawning an independent, non-interactive Hermes CLI child process (hermes chat \--query-file \<prompt\_file\>) with the HERMES\_TUI\_RESUME environment variable stripped and without \-c or \--continue flags, ensuring a clean session entry in \~/.hermes/state.db with zero prior conversational turns6. In accordance with the RinDig/agentless 54-word pointer benchmark, the runner passes a concise pointer instruction directing the agent to read AGENTS.md and stages/{stage\_name}/CONTEXT.md, load only the exact paths in Inputs, invoke read\_file before editing any existing file on disk, write deliverables to stages/{stage\_name}/output/, and terminate4.  
Once the stage compilation process exits, we enforce the RinDig/agentless Fresh Context Auditing rule (*"The context that generates an output must never grade that output"*)5. The runner erases the inference server KV cache, executes the stage's deterministic verification script (contract.sh) in a separate process, and writes the structured audit receipt to stages/{stage\_name}/output/check.md2. Only when contract.sh returns exit code 0 and output/check.md records auditor\_verdict: PASS does the runner evaluate output/checkpoint.md and advance to the next stage5.

### **4.2 Exact Mechanism for Clearing and Isolating KV Cache State in llama-server**

Spawning a fresh hermes chat \--query-file process isolates the client session history, but the underlying inference engine (llama-server on Port 8138\) retains state across HTTP requests in two locations: **GPU VRAM KV-Cache Slots** (--parallel N) and the **Host RAM Prompt Cache** (--cache-ram)3.  
Forensic documentation from the ggml-org/llama.cpp repository (Issues \#28139 and \#30961, and Discussion \#30746) highlights two caching behaviors that must be controlled during multi-stage runs12. First, by default llama-server assigns incoming requests to slots via Longest Common Prefix (LCP) similarity matching (-sps 0.5), which can cause subagent or subsequent stage prompts sharing the AGENTS.md prefix to collide on the same slot or fail unified KV-cache restoration (state\_seq\_set\_data: error loading state: failed to restore kv cache)47. Second, as documented in ggml-org/llama.cpp Discussion \#30746, when \--cache-ram is enabled (the default in llama-server), calling POST /slots/{id\_slot}?action=erase clears the GPU VRAM slot **but does not clear the host RAM cache**, causing the next request to reload cached tokens from host RAM12.  
To achieve complete KV-cache isolation between stage transitions without restarting llama-server (which would incur disk reload latency for the 4.8 GB GGUF model), we enforce a **Three-Point KV Cache Isolation Protocol**:

| Isolation Layer | Exact Parameter / Command | Technical Mechanism & Effect on RTX 3050 (Port 8138\) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. llama-server Daemon Flags** | \--port 8138 \-c 131072 \-ctk q4\_0 \-ctv q4\_0 \-np 1 \--slots \--cache-ram 0 \-sps 0.0 | Allocates 1 dedicated 128K TurboQuant Q4\_0 slot (id\_slot: 0), enables the /slots control API (--slots), disables similarity guessing (-sps 0.0), and disables host RAM prompt resurrection (--cache-ram 0\) so slot erasure is total3. |
| **2\. Inter-Stage Slot Purge API** | curl \-s \-X POST "http\://127.0.0.1:8138/slots/0?action=erase" \-H "Content-Type: application/json" | Executed by \_tools/hermes\_stage\_runner.py before Stage 1, between Stage k and its verification check, and before Stage k+1. Erases cached KV tokens in GPU VRAM while keeping model weights resident11. |
| **3\. Telemetry Verification** | Inspect timings.cache\_n \== 0 (or tokens\_cached \== 0\) on Turn 1 of each stage | Verifies that Turn 1 of every newly launched stage begins with zero cached KV tokens from prior stages11. |

### **4.3 Filesystem Representation of Checkpoints, Audits, and Human Reviews**

Grounded in \_core/CONVENTIONS.md (Convention 7: *Checkpoints* and Convention 8: *Stage audits*), RinDig/icm-architect (Invariant 6: *Every step ends at a check* and Invariant 9: *Status lives on disk*), and the practitioner findings reported by Van Clief & McDermott (arXiv:2603.16021v2), human oversight across a multi-stage compiler pipeline follows a **U-Shaped Human Intervention Curve**9. Across 33 practitioners using multi-stage ICM workflows (within a 52-member practitioner community, where 30 of 33 reported this U-shaped pattern), self-reported human edit frequency averaged **92% at Stage 1** (research, probing, and direction-setting), dropped to **30% at Stage 2** (constrained execution governed by Stage 1 outputs and Layer 3 reference rules), and rose to **78% at Stage 3** (final production assembly and debugging)10.  
![][image8]  
To represent both automated quality audits and human review gates directly on disk without external databases or proprietary dashboards, every stage directory stages/{NN}-{stage}/ writes three plain-text artifacts inside its output/ subdirectory2. First, the **Working Artifact (output/{deliverable})** (probe\_state.json, aim\_controller.py, telemetry.json) serves as a direct human edit surface per ICM Principle 4: a human engineer can open, edit, and save the file before the downstream stage runs, and the next stage reads whatever is on disk5. Second, the **Automated Audit Receipt (output/check.md)** is written by \_tools/hermes\_stage\_runner.py after executing the stage's contract.sh in a fresh process; if auditor\_verdict is FAIL, the pipeline stops immediately2. Third, the **Human Review Gate File (output/checkpoint.md)** records human approval state in YAML frontmatter13. In interactive mode (used when building new features, pausing at high-leverage Stage 1 and Stage 3 boundaries), output/checkpoint.md initializes to human\_decision: PENDING\_REVIEW until the engineer updates it to APPROVED or EDITED10. In autonomous mode (used for deterministic regression verification in make run-all-gauntlets), passing output/check.md (contract\_exit\_code: 0\) writes human\_decision: AUTO\_APPROVED\_BY\_CONTRACT to output/checkpoint.md and chains to the next stage1.

Save the following complete Python orchestrator (strictly under 60 lines, zero placeholders) to /var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes/\_tools/hermes\_stage\_runner.py2:

Python  
\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
"""Autonomous ICM Stage Compiler with llama-server KV Slot Isolation."""  
import argparse  
import datetime  
import json  
import os  
import subprocess  
import sys  
import urllib.request

def erase\_kv\_slot(base\_url: str \= "http\://127.0.0.1:8138") \-\> bool:  
    req \= urllib.request.Request(f"{base\_url}/slots/0?action=erase", method="POST",  
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, data=b"{}")  
    try:  
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=3) as resp:  
            return resp.status \== 200  
    except Exception:  
        return False

def run\_stage(stage\_dir: str, gate\_mode: str, skip\_llm: bool) \-\> int:  
    stage\_name \= os.path.basename(stage\_dir.rstrip("/"))  
    out\_dir \= os.path.join(stage\_dir, "output")  
    os.makedirs(out\_dir, exist\_ok=True)  
    kv\_erased \= erase\_kv\_slot()  
    if not skip\_llm:  
        prompt\_path \= os.path.join(out\_dir, ".compiler\_prompt.txt")  
        prompt \= (f"Read AGENTS.md and {stage\_dir}/CONTEXT.md. Load only the exact paths in Inputs. "  
                  f"Call read\_file before editing any existing file. Execute Process steps, write "  
                  f"deliverables to {out\_dir}/, and stop immediately.")  
        with open(prompt\_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
            f.write(prompt)  
        env \= {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k \!= "HERMES\_TUI\_RESUME"}  
        subprocess.run(\["hermes", "chat", "--query-file", prompt\_path\], env=env, check=True)  
        erase\_kv\_slot()  
    contract\_sh \= os.path.join(stage\_dir, "contract.sh")  
    rc \= subprocess.run(\["bash", contract\_sh\], check=False).returncode if os.path.exists(contract\_sh) else 0  
    now \= datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")  
    verdict \= "PASS" if rc \== 0 else "FAIL"  
    with open(os.path.join(out\_dir, "check.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
        f.write(f"---\\nstage\_id: \\"{stage\_name}\\"\\ntimestamp\_utc: \\"{now}\\"\\n"  
                f"kv\_slot\_erased: {str(kv\_erased).lower()}\\ncontract\_exit\_code: {rc}\\n"  
                f"auditor\_verdict: \\"{verdict}\\"\\n---\\n\# Audit: {verdict}\\n")  
    decision \= "AUTO\_APPROVED\_BY\_CONTRACT" if (gate\_mode \== "autonomous" and rc \== 0) else (  
               "APPROVED" if rc \== 0 else "REJECTED")  
    with open(os.path.join(out\_dir, "checkpoint.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
        f.write(f"---\\nstage\_id: \\"{stage\_name}\\"\\nhuman\_decision: \\"{decision}\\"\\n"  
                f"timestamp\_utc: \\"{now}\\"\\n---\\n\# Checkpoint: {decision}\\n")  
    print(json.dumps({"stage": stage\_name, "verdict": verdict, "checkpoint": decision, "kv\_erased": kv\_erased}))  
    return rc

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
    ap \= argparse.ArgumentParser()  
    ap.add\_argument("--stage-dir", required=True)  
    ap.add\_argument("--gate-mode", choices=\["autonomous", "interactive"\], default="autonomous")  
    ap.add\_argument("--verify-only", action="store\_true")  
    args \= ap.parse\_args()  
    sys.exit(run\_stage(args.stage\_dir, args.gate\_mode, args.verify\_only))

First, save the NVML / nvidia-smi hardware envelope verifier to /var/home/imshubhamsocial/Projects/Workspace/Personal/hermes/\_tools/check\_vram\_limit.py (strictly under 60 lines, zero placeholders)1:

Python  
\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
"""Deterministic NVIDIA RTX 3050 VRAM Ceiling & Quiescence Verifier."""  
import argparse  
import json  
import subprocess  
import sys

def check\_vram(mode: str, max\_active\_mib: float, max\_quiescent\_mib: float) \-\> int:  
    cmd \= \["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu,power.draw",  
           "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"\]  
    out \= subprocess.check\_output(cmd, text=True).strip().splitlines()\[0\]  
    parts \= \[p.strip() for p in out.split(",")\]  
    used\_mib \= float(parts\[0\])  
    total\_mib \= float(parts\[1\])  
    temp\_c \= float(parts\[2\])  
    power\_w \= float(parts\[3\]) if parts\[3\] \!= "\[N/A\]" else 0.0  
    ceiling \= max\_quiescent\_mib if mode \== "quiescent" else max\_active\_mib  
    passed \= used\_mib \<= ceiling  
    receipt \= {  
        "mode": mode,  
        "vram\_used\_mib": used\_mib,  
        "vram\_total\_mib": total\_mib,  
        "ceiling\_mib": ceiling,  
        "headroom\_mib": round(ceiling \- used\_mib, 1),  
        "temperature\_c": temp\_c,  
        "power\_w": power\_w,  
        "passed": passed  
    }  
    print(json.dumps(receipt))  
    return 0 if passed else 1

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
    ap \= argparse.ArgumentParser()  
    ap.add\_argument("--mode", choices=\["active", "quiescent"\], default="quiescent")  
    ap.add\_argument("--max-active", type\=float, default=5800.0)  
    ap.add\_argument("--max-quiescent", type\=float, default=100.0)  
    args \= ap.parse\_args()  
    sys.exit(check\_vram(args.mode, args.max\_active, args.max\_quiescent))

Python  
\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
"""Automated 8-Point ICM Walk Test and Workspace Contract Validator."""  
import json  
import os  
import re  
import sys

ROOT \= os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(\_\_file\_\_)))

def count\_lines(path: str) \-\> int:  
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
        return len(f.readlines())

def validate\_workspace() \-\> int:  
    errors \= \[\]  
    agents\_md \= os.path.join(ROOT, "AGENTS.md")  
    context\_md \= os.path.join(ROOT, "CONTEXT.md")  
    invariants\_md \= os.path.join(ROOT, "\_config", "invariants.md")  
    for req in \[agents\_md, context\_md, invariants\_md\]:  
        if not os.path.isfile(req):  
            errors.append(f"Missing core file: {req}")  
    if os.path.isfile(agents\_md) and count\_lines(agents\_md) \> 60:  
        errors.append("Layer 0 AGENTS.md exceeds 60-line limit")  
    if os.path.isfile(context\_md) and count\_lines(context\_md) \> 80:  
        errors.append("Layer 1 CONTEXT.md exceeds 80-line limit")  
    for ptr in \["CLAUDE.md", "IDENTITY.md"\]:  
        p \= os.path.join(ROOT, ptr)  
        if os.path.isfile(p) and count\_lines(p) \> 5:  
            errors.append(f"{ptr} must be a 1-line pointer to AGENTS.md (One Fact, One Home)")  
    stage\_dirs \= \["stages/01-probe", "stages/02-controller", "stages/03-execute",  
                  "benchmarks/gauntlet\_a\_voxel\_fps", "benchmarks/gauntlet\_b\_splatbox",  
                  "benchmarks/gauntlet\_c\_aquarium"\]  
    for sd in stage\_dirs:  
        cpath \= os.path.join(ROOT, sd, "CONTEXT.md")  
        if not os.path.isfile(cpath):  
            errors.append(f"Missing stage contract: {sd}/CONTEXT.md")  
            continue  
        if count\_lines(cpath) \> 80:  
            errors.append(f"{sd}/CONTEXT.md exceeds 80-line limit")  
        with open(cpath, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
            txt \= f.read()  
        for sec in \["\#\# Inputs", "\#\# Process", "\#\# Outputs", "\#\# Check"\]:  
            if sec not in txt:  
                errors.append(f"{sd}/CONTEXT.md missing required section: {sec}")  
        for rel in re.findall(r"\`(\\.\\./\[^\`\]+)\`", txt):  
            target \= os.path.normpath(os.path.join(ROOT, sd, rel))  
            if not os.path.exists(target):  
                errors.append(f"Broken relative link in {sd}/CONTEXT.md: {rel}")  
    report \= {"walk\_test\_passed": len(errors) \== 0, "error\_count": len(errors), "errors": errors}  
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))  
    return 0 if len(errors) \== 0 else 1

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
    sys.exit(validate\_workspace())
